questions.question: Which international standard governs the determination of apparent density and mass per unit area of leather, and what is its fundamental test principle?

answers.a: ISO 5402; cyclic flex cracking under repeated angular deflection
answers.b: ISO 2420 (IUP 4); treating a circular test disc as a regular cylinder to compute envelope volume from thickness and surface area, and dividing conditioned mass by volume
answers.c: ISO 11640; assessing surface color fastness to reciprocal rubbing cycles
answers.d: ISO 3376; measuring tensile breaking strength and elongation at break

questions.question: What is the key scientific distinction between the 'apparent density' (bulk density) of leather and the 'true density' of its solid collagen matrix?

answers.a: Apparent density is measured at 100°C, whereas true density is measured at absolute zero
answers.b: Apparent density accounts for both the solid tanning-collagen network and internal void/pore volume, whereas true density (approx. 1.35 to 1.42 g/cm³) excludes all pores
answers.c: True density measures the mass per unit surface area, while apparent density measures tensile modulus
answers.d: Apparent density applies only to synthetic polymers, whereas true density applies to natural hides

questions.question: Why does ISO 2419 mandate conditioning leather specimens at 20 ± 2°C and 65 ± 2% RH for at least 24 hours prior to mass and dimension measurements?

answers.a: To fully denature the fibrous triple helix of collagen protein
answers.b: To establish thermodynamic moisture sorption equilibrium, eliminating mass and swelling variations caused by the hygroscopic hysteresis of polar collagen peptide groups
answers.c: To completely evaporate all volatile tanning syntans and residual fatliquors
answers.d: To sterilize the leather against anaerobic bacterial biodeterioration during testing

questions.question: According to ISO 2420, what is the nominal diameter and geometry of the circular test specimen cut by the steel press knife?
In accordance with ISO 2589, what specific contact pressure and presser foot dimensions must be applied when measuring the thickness of compressible leather?

answers.a: Pressure of 10.0 ± 0.5 kPa with a 5.0 mm spherical anvil
answers.b: Pressure of 49.1 ± 1.0 kPa (approx. 393 g dead mass) across a flat circular presser foot of 10.00 mm diameter
answers.c: Pressure of 100.0 ± 5.0 kPa across a pointed conical tip of 1.0 mm radius
answers.d: Variable spring pressure ranging from 20 kPa to 200 kPa depending on leather stiffness

questions.question: In the ISO 2420 multi-point thickness protocol, where are the four designated measurement points located on the 70 mm circular specimen?

answers.a: Four evenly spaced points positioned along the extreme outer circumference
answers.b: One central point (T₁) and three peripheral points (T₂, T₃, T₄) positioned 20.0 mm from the center forming an equilateral triangle
answers.c: Four points aligned in a single straight diametrical line across the grain
answers.d: Two points on the flesh side and two points on the grain side chosen at random

questions.question: Why does ISO 2420 mandate measuring the diameter of the circular specimen along two mutually perpendicular directions (rotated by 90°)?

answers.a: To calibrate the zero baseline of the Vernier caliper between readings
answers.b: To account for specimen ovality caused by anisotropic viscoelastic recovery and differential fiber bundle orientation (Langer's lines) during die cutting
answers.c: To verify that the temperature has remained constant between cuts
answers.d: To test whether the cutting die has magnetized the leather matrix

questions.question: How is the internal void fraction (porosity, ε) of leather mathematically related to its apparent density (ρ) and true collagen density (ρ_t)?
From which mathematical derivation does the numerical constant 1.273 × 10⁶ arise in the ISO 2420 apparent density formula ρ = (1.273 × 10⁶ × m) / (t × d²)?

answers.a: From the acceleration due to gravity (g = 9.80665 m/s²) multiplied by ambient air density
answers.b: From (4 / π) ≈ 1.27324 combined with conversion factors relating grams to kilograms (10⁻³) and cubic millimeters to cubic meters (10⁻⁹)
answers.c: From the moisture absorption isotherm coefficient at 65% relative humidity
answers.d: From the calibration ratio between the presser foot area and specimen surface area

questions.question: Which of the following leather types typically exhibits the highest apparent density, and what structural feature accounts for this?

answers.a: Milled lambskin garment nappa; due to loosely braided reticular collagen fibers
answers.b: Vegetable-tanned sole leather; due to heavy filling with vegetable polyphenolic tannins, dense fiber compaction, and mechanical rolling
answers.c: Chrome-tanned suede split; due to open interstitial voids and lack of grain layer
answers.d: Automotive upholstery leather; due to micro-cellular polyurethane foam backing
